page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the c3d server family. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor using x86_64 architecture with multithreading enabled. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of dedicated system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPU hardware.

The underlying AMD EPYC processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16, and cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. In performance testing, the server demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% of benchmarks. Multi-core performance, software compilation, and ray tracing benchmarks fall within the average range.

While cached memory bandwidth is average at 565.97 GB/sec, uncached large-block memory read and write speeds are weak, measuring 37.36 GB/sec and 14.86 GB/sec respectively. This indicates a potential bottleneck for memory-intensive workloads operating on large datasets. However, the server maintains average performance for static web serving, database operations, and small-scale LLM inference, though performance drops significantly on larger models.

Given its balanced resource allocation and dedicated CPU cores, the c3d-standard-8 offers a stable, cost-efficient profile for general-purpose computing without the overhead of specialized hardware. It is suited for workloads such as web serving, software compilation, moderate database operations, and lightweight text or image processing.
